research_record.identity: Eduard Tubin, Sonata for alto saxophone and piano, ETW 61, completed March 9, 1951. The composer also authorized viola. Current retail edition NMS1998, Gehrmans, issued 1993.
research_record.findings: Freshly downloaded BIS-CD-269 booklet identifies the original alto saxophone recording by Pekka Savijoki and Roland Pöntinen, with movements Allegro, Adagio and Allegro vivace. Its timings are 5:59, 4:41 and 3:24, total 14:07. Harri Kiisk’s booklet note describes development of the saxophone’s initial theme against the piano’s dance music. Virtuosic saxophone runs lead without a break into the Adagio, based on a thirteenth-century troubadour song. The middle section moves faster and recalls the Sixth Symphony’s tenor-saxophone motif. The finale exchanges a second theme between piano and saxophone, broadens at the climax and concludes with a virtuoso rush. Eino Tubin’s 2017 biography says the slow movement began as a freestanding cello piece, Troubadour Song from the 13th Century. It also reports Tobias Lund’s recognition of a middle-movement motif from Judy Garland’s On the Bumpy Road to Love and the composer’s manuscript permission to perform on viola. The two freshly read primary sources disagree on the first complete performance day: BIS says September 23, 1951; Eino Tubin’s biography says September 22. Both give Jules de Vries and Martin Keil in Uppsala. The discrepancy should remain visible. June Emerson’s exact NMS1998 record confirms alto saxophone or viola with piano, Gehrmans, issue 1993 and ISMN M661541998. Issue 1993 is not the original composition year. Virgo Veldi and Johan Randvere’s full video is supplied from Randvere’s channel and linked by the Tubin Society. The caption identifies a 2015 live recording in Tubin Hall, Tartu and gives all three movement starts. Browser playback was verified.
